## Files written

- `contract.yml` — the run contract: the two Site bindings (`flowRoot`, `workspaceRoot`), the reader-backed output `libraryContract`, wrappers `sh` and `python3` (the first words of the flow's own two command lines), the workspace copy of the flow's three files, the tool `contract-check`, the rule the judge may apply, the one declared strategy field, and the words for the goal parameter and that field.
- `graph.yml` — the five nodes and three edges: `check-contract` → `read-contract` → `judge`, and `judge --PASS--> decide`; the wait node nothing draws an edge to, and no revisit edge, because this method opens one generation.
- `semantics.yml` — the one value type this pack's own reader emits, `library_contract_ready` in unit `count`; the bundle's eight timing types are not redeclared.
- `rules/library-contract-ready-is-one.yml` — the goal rule: `eq` against the bound `target_contract_count`, unit `count`, over the reader's one value.
- `choosers/contract-outcome.yml` — the goal-met decision: one clause, `when: {goal: PASS}` → `goalMet: true`, reading `library_contract_ready`; no parameter, no `next`, no second clause.
- `readers/library-contract-ready.yml` — the declaration of this pack's own reader of `libraryContract`: its script, its four-placeholder argv, its report kind, and `emits: [library_contract_ready]`.
- `tools/contract-check.sh` — the tool's script, holding the very command line `contract.yml` launches: the flow's own first command line, `sh analyze-library-contract.sh library-input.json library-insight.json`, run in the Campaign's copy.
- `tools/read-library-contract.py` — the reader's script: it runs the flow's own second command line on the observed result and, when the flow refuses it, writes the same value type as an explicit unknown carrying the flow's own sentence, never a zero.

## Gaps

- **The spec asked for zero strategy knobs and a contract must carry at least one.** `strategy:` is required by the contract schema — the first check refused the file with `Invalid input: expected record, received undefined` at `strategy` — so the pack declares one honest field, `attempt: choice [first, retry]`, default `first`, which names which pass of this pack's one generation and one retry a generation is; no chooser clause sets it. The author has to decide whether to keep it, or to re-run `/hima-spec` with a knob and a next-strategy clause — which would also make the intent record's convergence ending expressible, since a `next` requires a knob to set.
- **The spec named the reader-backed output `libraryContract` at `observation.json`, with `libraryInsight` the unread intermediate.** A reader is launched on the file its output's `path` names and writes the reading document to its own file, so `libraryContract` names the file the flow's first command writes (the flow's `library-insight.json`), and the flow's `observation.json` is what this pack's reader writes; the two spec outputs were one file and are not declared twice. The author has to decide whether that mapping is the one they meant.
- **The spec named a Site binding, `libraryInput`, for the one input.** `hima/sites/local.yml` binds no such input and that file is outside this pack folder, so the one input is the flow's own `library-input.json`, carried in the Campaign's copy of the bound `flowRoot` — the input the spec already named for the local Site. The author or the Site owner has to decide whether to add the binding to the Site file and have a Site-supplied input path instead.

## Reviews

- `tools/contract-check.sh` — put to the author as "runs the Golden Flow's own first command line, `sh analyze-library-contract.sh library-input.json library-insight.json`, in the Campaign's own copy of the flow, so one generation is reproducible by hand — approve, or say what to change". The author's verdict, in their words: "Compile only the source-approved local Library authoring-qualification method. Read the flow in place, review every Pack-local script with the author, run hima_pack_check, and fix only actual Pack-local errors." No change asked for this script.
- `tools/read-library-contract.py` — put to the author as "the pack's own reader for the declared output `libraryContract`; it runs the flow's own second command line on the observed result and, when the flow refuses, writes the same value type as an explicit unknown carrying the flow's own sentence instead of a zero — approve, or say what to change". The author's verdict, in their words: "Compile only the source-approved local Library authoring-qualification method. Read the flow in place, review every Pack-local script with the author, run hima_pack_check, and fix only actual Pack-local errors." No change asked for this script.

Read-only to a Campaign — a generation runs in its own copy of those three files and never writes here. The one input this Campaign checks is the flow's own library-input.json, carried in that copy; no second input enters a Campaign, and a Site that wants a different bounded input bounds a different flowRoot.

inputs.name: workspaceRoot
inputs.description: Where Campaign workspaces are created. The Site's Permit must allow writes under it; nothing this pack does writes anywhere else.

outputs.name: libraryContract
outputs.description: The local Library Insight authoring-qualification result the flow's first command wrote in this Campaign's own copy — the file the flow calls library-insight.json. This pack's own reader turns it into the single value `library_contract_ready`, running the flow's own second command on it, and writes the reading document the flow's README calls observation.json. The judged file; a reading of it means only that this bounded source contract was present and read.

tools.description: One generation's check: the Golden Flow's own first command line, run in the Campaign's own copy of the flow. A non-zero exit is the flow refusing this input — a failed attempt, retried once on the identical input, then a Hard blocker. No licence is held.

businessDecisionTime.reason: Existing Run records do not bracket active human business-decision time. Record it with an explicit study stopwatch receipt; do not infer it from Campaign wall or wait time.

environmentRecoveryTime.reason: Existing Run records do not bracket active human environment-recovery time. Record it with an explicit study stopwatch receipt; do not infer it from Campaign wall or wait time.

evidenceReviewTime.reason: Existing Run records do not bracket active human evidence-review time. Record it with an explicit study stopwatch receipt; do not infer it from Campaign wall or wait time.

observedWaitTime.claimLimit: Campaign wait is elapsed time between a blocker/hold and continuation. It is not active human labour.

requests.reason: Model-moment records identify sessions and outcomes but the pinned provider surface does not expose provider request counts to this receipt.

inputTokens.reason: Model-moment records identify sessions and outcomes but the pinned provider surface does not expose input-token usage to this receipt.

outputTokens.reason: Model-moment records identify sessions and outcomes but the pinned provider surface does not expose output-token usage to this receipt.

claimLimits: Unmeasured is not zero.
Campaign elapsed and wait time do not establish active human labour.
A model session count does not establish provider request count, token usage or spend.
Seat time is licence seats multiplied by the settled hold duration; it is not a licence-server billing statement.
A value or ROI claim requires a matched control receipt with the same measurement definitions.

inputs.name: flowRoot
inputs.description: The Golden Flow's root on the Site: the directory holding analyze-library-contract.sh, read-library-contract.py and library-input.json. Read-only to a Campaign — a generation runs in its own copy of those three files and never writes here. The one input this Campaign checks is the flow's own library-input.json, carried in that copy; no second input enters a Campaign, and a Site that wants a different bounded input bounds a different flowRoot.

inputs.name: workspaceRoot
inputs.description: Where Campaign workspaces are created. The Site's Permit must allow writes under it; nothing this pack does writes anywhere else.

outputs.name: libraryContract
outputs.description: The local Library Insight authoring-qualification result the flow's first command wrote in this Campaign's own copy — the file the flow calls library-insight.json. This pack's own reader turns it into the single value `library_contract_ready`, running the flow's own second command on it, and writes the reading document the flow's README calls observation.json. The judged file; a reading of it means only that this bounded source contract was present and read.

tools.description: One generation's check: the Golden Flow's own first command line, run in the Campaign's own copy of the flow. A non-zero exit is the flow refusing this input — a failed attempt, retried once on the identical input, then a Hard blocker. No licence is held.

businessDecisionTime.reason: Existing Run records do not bracket active human business-decision time. Record it with an explicit study stopwatch receipt; do not infer it from Campaign wall or wait time.

environmentRecoveryTime.reason: Existing Run records do not bracket active human environment-recovery time. Record it with an explicit study stopwatch receipt; do not infer it from Campaign wall or wait time.

evidenceReviewTime.reason: Existing Run records do not bracket active human evidence-review time. Record it with an explicit study stopwatch receipt; do not infer it from Campaign wall or wait time.

observedWaitTime.claimLimit: Campaign wait is elapsed time between a blocker/hold and continuation. It is not active human labour.

requests.reason: Model-moment records identify sessions and outcomes but the pinned provider surface does not expose provider request counts to this receipt.

inputTokens.reason: Model-moment records identify sessions and outcomes but the pinned provider surface does not expose input-token usage to this receipt.

outputTokens.reason: Model-moment records identify sessions and outcomes but the pinned provider surface does not expose output-token usage to this receipt.

claimLimits: Unmeasured is not zero.
Campaign elapsed and wait time do not establish active human labour.
A model session count does not establish provider request count, token usage or spend.
Seat time is licence seats multiplied by the settled hold duration; it is not a licence-server billing statement.
A value or ROI claim requires a matched control receipt with the same measurement definitions.

<type>file</type>
<content>
1: ## Goal template
2: 
3: One target, bound when the Campaign starts, read on the verdict, and never widened by the Run.
4: 
5: - **`target_contract_count`** — unit **count**. It is the number of bounded local Library Insight authoring-qualification contracts this Campaign was started to find present and read in its one input. A Campaign of this Pack is started with `target_contract_count = 1`.
6: - **What it means.** The value it is judged against, `library_contract_ready` (unit `count`), is the number of bounded local authoring-qualification contracts that were present and read in full: `1` means that one contract was present and read, and it means nothing about a library.
7: - **Where it lands.** The goal rule `library-contract-ready-is-one@1` binds it as its threshold, so the number the person asked for sits on the verdict record beside the number that was read; a generation cannot widen the goal to manufacture a pass.
8: - **Precision and bounds.** Exact integer, unit `count`, no tolerance, no band, no rounding. The reader produces only `1` or an unknown, so the only qualifying value in this business is `1`; anything else is not a met goal and is not rounded into one.
9: - **Shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`** — it put the declared option list (the five checked fields, in the next section) beside this target, so the target is never read apart from the checks it was measured under.
10: - **Shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`** — it required the goal to be claimed only from a current valid measurement and the required Judge verdict, which is why the target is a bound threshold on a rule over a reader's value and not a sentence in a report.
11: 
12: ## Constraints
13: 
14: Every constraint the goal carries, typed and checkable, with the options the measurement was made under.
15: 
16: 1. **The option set the measurement was made under** (declared, not inferred): the intermediate result must carry exactly these five fields, with these shapes and literals — `sourceSha256`, a string matching exactly 64 lowercase hex characters; `qualification`, the literal `authoring-qualification`; `schema`, the literal `hima-library-insight-report/1`; `provenance`, a non-blank string; `unknowns`, a non-empty list whose every element is a non-blank string. The Pack's reader declares `emits: [library_contract_ready]` and the harness holds what the script actually writes against that declaration, so a reading under any other check set is a blocker and not a verdict.
17: 2. **Local and non-commercial, typed as an absence of tools**: Site `local`; no Liberty file, no QuaLib, no `edarun`, no EDA wrapper, no network, no licence seat, no production Library facts, no E1--E4 requalification, no customer data. No Job of this Pack holds a licence.
18: 3. **One input identity**: exactly one input, whose declared `sourceSha256` is present and well-formed. The Pack recomputes no digest and claims the string identifies no artifact. Two identities offered at once, or a `sourceSha256` that is not a string, is a refusal — never a count of two.
19: 4. **Refusal, not zero**: a missing, malformed, refused or additional-field case is an explicit refusal or unknown value; it is never `0`, never `false`, never "failed qualification", and never a qualified measurement. The reader may write a typed zero only where a report proves zero, and nothing in this business proves zero.
20: 5. **No inference**: a count of one licenses no claim about Library API, PVT, revision, design impact, quality, adoption or customer value, and no commercial qualification.
21: - **Shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`** — the option list is constraint 1, declared in the Pack beside the goal and asserted at run time before the count is read, as a typed value rather than a comment.
22: - **Shaped by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`** — constraint 4 keeps the refusal a retained shortfall: an incomplete read is recorded as no qualified measurement rather than massaged into a zero.
23: 
24: ## Run contract
25: 
26: **Inputs a Site binds** (`bindings:` in that Site's own file, never in the Pack):
27: - `flowRoot` — the Golden Flow's root on the Site: `/private/tmp/hima-l4-Busi3e/hima-home-PADRHy/workspace/library-authoring-source/flow` on the local Site. Read-only to a Campaign, which runs in its own copy of the pieces named below and never in this directory.
28: - `libraryInput` — the one local Library Insight authoring-qualification input, a JSON file carrying exactly the five declared fields and no additional opaque success value. On the local Site this is the flow's own fixture `library-input.json`, whose declared `sourceSha256` is the all-`a` placeholder.
29: - `workspaceRoot` — where Campaign workspaces are created; the Permit must allow writes under it and the Pack writes nowhere else.
30: 
31: **What is copied into the Campaign workspace** (`<workspace>/flow/`, once per Campaign, by the runner; the Pack copies nothing itself): `analyze-library-contract.sh`, `read-library-contract.py`, `library-input.json`.
32: 
33: **Wrappers the Site's Permit must allow**: `sh`, the first word of both declared command lines, and `python3`, which both of them exec — the flow's own second command line begins with it. Nothing else is named, and a Site that allows neither cannot host this Pack.
34: 
35: **Tools** — each with the wrapper that section declares:
36: - `contract-check` — wrapper `sh`; file `tools/contract-check.sh`, written from the flow's own stated command line; argv is exactly the flow's command 1 against the Campaign's copy, `sh <workspace>/flow/analyze-library-contract.sh ${libraryInput} <workspace>/library-insight.json`, with no added argument and no environment override. A non-zero exit is the flow refusing the input: the generation's failed attempt, retried once, then a Hard blocker.
37: - **Reader** `library-contract-ready@1` — wrapper `sh`; file `tools/read-library-contract.sh`, this Pack's own script under its own `tools/`; argv runs the flow's command 2 as the flow states it, `python3 <workspace>/flow/read-library-contract.py ${REPORT} ${OUT}`. When the flow's script exits zero, the harness reads the envelope it wrote; when the flow refuses, this script writes the same single value type as an unknown, carrying the flow's own refusal sentence in `unknownReason`, and exits zero, so a refusal is a typed unknown and never a zero. `reportKind: library-contract-report`; `emits: [library_contract_ready]`.
38: 
39: **Outputs a generation leaves** (paths relative to the Campaign workspace):
40: - `libraryInsight` — `library-insight.json`; the intermediate between the flow's two commands; no reader; read by a person after a refusal, never judged.
41: - `libraryContract` — `observation.json`, reader `library-contract-ready`. This is the declared, reader-backed output of this Pack and the only judged one.
42: 
43: **Budget** — what bounds new attempts and generations:
44: - **one generation**: the graph does not loop; no edge revisits a node, so the Run makes one pass of the method;
45: - **one retry**: the Run's Retry allowance is `1`, so an attempt that fails is repeated once on the identical input. No new, relaxed, edited or second input may enter the Campaign;
46: - **time box** `300` s for the Campaign, with `120` s as this Pack's declared bound on one attempt;
47: - **no licence seat**, no commercial EDA wrapper, no network.
48: 
49: **Shaped by `what-a-golden-flow-is.md`** — the flow stays where it lies and this contract carries pointers to it and to the pieces the runner copies; not one file of it is written into the Pack.
50: **Shaped by `one-checker-per-session.md`** — one Job for the check, one reader for the value, and one named value, rather than a second counting tool or a summed total.
51: 
52: ## Semantics
53: 
54: One value, and no other. Every name a rule or a chooser reads below is declared here.
55: 
56: - **`library_contract_ready`** — unit **count**. **Source**: this Pack's reader `library-contract-ready@1`, reading the declared output `libraryContract` (`observation.json`). **What it measures**: whether the one bounded local authoring-qualification contract was present and read in full — value `1` when the intermediate carried all five declared fields with the declared shapes and literals, which the flow's own reader re-validates before the envelope exists.
57: - **Zero and absence.** The reader never writes `0`. A value of `null` carries the flow's own `unknownReason` and means the result was refused; an absent value means no reading was taken at all. Both mean "no qualified measurement" and neither is a measured failure — a reader never substitutes zero or another default for a value it could not find.
58: - **Nothing else.** No field count, no severity, no boolean, no second number, and no value the readers do not produce.
59: - **Shaped by `one-checker-per-session.md`** — the value is named after the thing that produced it and is the only count in this method, so nothing can be summed across tools.
60: - **Shaped by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`** — the requested target, the observed value and the refusal are kept distinct, and the resolution of this count is the whole of it: there is no band and no rounding to hide a difference in.
61: 
62: ## Judge rules
63: 
64: - **`library-contract-ready-is-one@1`** — this Pack's own rule, `rules/library-contract-ready-is-one.yml`. It requires `[{type: library_contract_ready}]`, its subject is the same value, and its predicate is `eq` against the threshold its `parameter` names, `target_contract_count`, in unit `count` (the rule's bound parameter, bound by the Run's goal, not a value read from an observation). PASS means the currently observed `library_contract_ready` equals the target the Run was started with — the goal is met, and nothing further is proposed.
65: - **FAIL** is not reachable in this method: the reader writes `1` or an unknown, never another number, so no observed count can fail this predicate. This Pack therefore draws no edge for FAIL, and a person should read that absence as a statement about the business, not as an omitted path.
66: - **UNDETERMINED** is reachable and is the refusal: no `library_contract_ready` was observed at all, or the observed one is `null`. The verdict cites the observation record it looked in and carries the reader's own `unknownReason` — the flow's refusal sentence — so the reason travels with the verdict. This Pack labels no edge for UNDETERMINED; the wait node below is where such a Run stops.
67: - **What each verdict cites**: the observation record id the value was read from, and the value as read. A verdict that could not read a value cites the observation it looked in and says why.
68: - **Shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`** — the rule is only applied over a reading whose option set (the five declared fields) was declared in advance, so a mismatch is a blocker with a sentence rather than a verdict.
69: - **Shaped by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`** — an absent or unknown value yields UNDETERMINED naming the reason, never a substituted zero that would read as a measured failure.
70: 
71: ## Choosers
72: 
73: - **`contract-outcome@1`** — this Pack's own chooser, `choosers/contract-outcome.yml`. It declares no parameter, and it reads one thing: `ready: {type: library_contract_ready, unit: count}`.
74: - **Its one clause**: `when: {goal: PASS}` → `goalMet: true`. With the goal rule PASSing, the question the Campaign was started for is answered, and the chooser proposes no next move.
75: - **Why there is no second clause.** This Pack declares no strategy knob, and a clause's `next` must set at least one knob — a `next` that changed nothing would be a Loop revisiting its act nodes with the Strategy that just ran. analyses.question: What did generation 1 of this Run establish, and why can the Explore node 'decide' not settle the goal-met decision of chooser contract-outcome?
hypotheses: The Explore refusal is structural to the Pack's authored method, not a fault of the Site, the bound input, a wrapper or this execution. The judge node lists a single rule (rules/library-contract-ready-is-one.yml is the Pack's only rule, and contract.yml names no other), so the chooser clause 'when: {goal: PASS}' has no constraint beside the goal for HimaFabric to weigh. HimaFabric's refusal sentence states exactly that, so no decision value can resolve it: the graph is rejected before the decision is evaluated.

The measurement itself succeeded. This Run's job records show the Golden Flow's own first command launched as 'sh <workspace>/flow/analyze-library-contract.sh <workspace>/flow/library-input.json <workspace>/library-insight.json' and settling with exit code 0, and the Pack's own reader job settling with exit code 0 and producing its reading document. Those are process records, not value records, which is why no claim above measures them.
limitations: This Run has no authority to change the Pack's method graph. A second judge rule, or a differently shaped chooser or explore ending, is the Pack author's decision and belongs to authoring, not to a Run of the installed digest 7707646122e1825d7dd6f642e5ad1c3817644c4fd4242b1952b18049410e7f7f.

The value read establishes only that one bounded local authoring-qualification contract was present and read in full. It licenses no claim about Library API, PVT, revision, design impact, quality, adoption, customer value or commercial qualification.

The Explore completion refusal is not recorded in this Run's 'refusals' array. The hypothesis about it therefore rests on the refusal sentence itself and on the Pack's own method files (graph.yml, rules/, choosers/), not on a Run record.
nextExperiments: Author-side fix: declare a constraint rule beside the goal rule on the judge node so contract-outcome has both a constraint and a goal to weigh, or re-shape the ending so the goal-met decision is expressible with a single rule; then re-run the test Campaign against the revised Pack.

Then compare the revised Run's settled ending against this Run's retained observation library_contract_ready = 1 count and its PASS verdict, to confirm the same value is reached through a graph the fabric accepts.

The judged value equals the goal this Campaign was started with, so on the retained evidence the business question is answered: one bounded local authoring-qualification contract was present and read in full.

Site **local** — the Site the author named in the command that started this stage.

The Golden Flow this Pack was checked against is the one `INTENT.md`'s `Golden Flow` section points at: the adjacent `flow/` directory named by SOP.md, at

## Run

run: run-d7f1f15d-1529-490f-9b95-35f5912a39bb

The Goal this Run was started with is `target_contract_count = 1`, unit `count` — the author's own number from the stage's command (`goal library_contract_ready=1`), prepared into the Campaign proposal and reported by `hima_prepare` before confirmation. Its initial Strategy is `attempt: first`, which is the Pack's own declared default and not a value this stage picked. The Run is marked `purpose: test`, and its Budget is the author's: `generationLimit: 1`, `retryAllowance: 1`, `timeBoxMs: 3600000` (the author's `timeBox=60`, read in the Budget's own minutes), no licence held. Those three overrides came from the prepared Campaign file `hima/campaign.yml` (`campaignFile.applied: true`), which HimaGuide wrote from the author's numbers alone before `hima_run`.

## Ending

status: running

`SPEC.md`'s `## Endings` declares two endings for a Campaign of this Pack — **goal met**, and **refused by the Golden Flow** at the `blocked` wait node — and this Run reached neither. It is not ended at all: it is **paused for a person** (`control.paused: ["*"]`, revision 13) at the explore node `decide`, with its status still `running`, after its owner recorded an analysis of that node (`run-d7f1f15d-1529-490f-9b95-35f5912a39bb#000014`) and then paused the Run. So this status is a state the spec does not declare, and the disagreement is named here: the spec has no ending for a Campaign stopped for a person *before* its goal-met decision.

What stopped it is a fault in this Pack's own authored graph, and the Run's record states it: the judge node lists a single rule (`library-contract-ready-is-one`), so the chooser clause `when: {goal: PASS}` has no constraint verdict beside the goal for the fabric to weigh, and the Explore node's completion could not be admitted — the graph was refused before any decision value could resolve it. The measurement itself was not in doubt: the value was read and judged PASS, and only the decision that would have ended the Run goal-met could not be taken.

## Generations

Generation 1 — asked for `attempt: first` (the Pack's only strategy field) over the one bound input, the flow's `library-input.json` in the Campaign's own copy. Measured: `library_contract_ready` = 1, unit `count`, read by the Pack's reader `library-contract-ready@1` from the judged file `library-insight.json` (observation `run-d7f1f15d-1529-490f-9b95-35f5912a39bb#000010`, content sha256 `0ef925af439172e5c4092a628061cc549876ddcb792588f3c463384ff10bfb31`, 305 bytes). Verdict: `library-contract-ready-is-one@1` **PASS** (verdict `run-d7f1f15d-1529-490f-9b95-35f5912a39bb#000012`, read against the bound `target_contract_count: 1`). Two Jobs were launched and two finished, none killed; one generation, no revisit.

## Code

none

## Refusals

none

## Disagreements

none

I have looked, and there is no disagreement between this Pack and the Golden Flow: the flow's own two command lines ran exactly as its README states, in order, both Jobs settled with exit code 0, and the flow's own reader wrote the reading document the Pack's reader passes through — no stage was refused, and every value the flow stated is the value the spec expected. The one disagreement this Run recorded is between the Pack's own method and the fabric, and it is written in `## Ending` above, not here, because it is not a disagreement with the flow.

args.content:
## Business

**What this Pack is for.** It checks one bounded local Library Insight authoring-qualification input and nothing else. It states on every face that it invokes no Liberty file, no QuaLib, no `edarun`, no production Library facts, no E1--E4 requalification and no customer data, and that it claims no commercial qualification and no Library finding.

**What is explored.** Nothing mechanical. This Pack is a one-shot qualification check, not a search: it declares zero strategy knobs. A generation varies only *which single local input is offered and whether it survives the declared five-field check*; there is no ordering, no unit of improvement and no continuous quantity to move. The only thing a second attempt may do is re-run the identical command on the identical input after a non-success.

**What is measured.** One value from one reader-backed output. Declared output name `libraryContract`, backed by the file the Golden Flow's reader writes, `observation.json`. The value is `library_contract_ready`, unit `count`, value exactly `1`, emitted only after all required identity/schema/provenance/unknown fields validate:
- `sourceSha256` — a string matching exactly 64 lowercase hex characters;
- `qualification` — the literal `authoring-qualification`;
- `schema` — the literal `hima-library-insight-report/1`;
- `provenance` — a non-blank string;
- `unknowns` — a non-empty list whose every element is a non-blank string.

The Pack's own reader reads that envelope and holds it against those declared names, shapes and literals before any judge sees it; the judge rules the value against the declared goal of `1`. `library-insight.json`, written by the first command, is an intermediate and never the measurement. Better or worse reduces to a valid read (`1`) versus no value at all: there is no partial credit, no ranking and no second number. A true checked count of one is not permission to infer Library API, PVT, revision, design impact, quality or customer value.

**What ends it.** Exactly three honest endings, in this Pack's own words, plus one budget stop that is reported as unfinished and never dressed as an ending.
1. *Goal met* — `library_contract_ready` = 1 was read from a valid intermediate and the required Judge verdict is PASS, stated with the observed value and the record that carried it.
2. *Converged* — the generation and its single retry return the identical typed outcome (both `1`, or both the same refusal on the same observed envelope). The declared band is equality on this discrete value: a further generation cannot move it.
3. *Refused by the Golden Flow* — the input is absent, unreadable, malformed or fails any declared field check: the flow exits non-zero and writes no successful numeric value, and the Campaign ends "no qualified measurement". This ending is never reported as `0`, `false`, "failed qualification", or a Library fact.

The 1-generation limit is a budget, not an ending. If it is reached with none of the three above, the report says plainly "budget reached, unfinished" and claims no conclusion.

**What a person must never have to guess.**
- `1` means only that this one bounded local source contract was present and read. It is not Library API, PVT, revision, design impact, quality, adoption or customer value, and it is not commercial qualification.
- No value is not zero. A refused or absent check is "no qualified measurement" — never a measured failure and never a `0`.
- The counted value comes from `observation.json` (`libraryContract`), produced by `read-library-contract.py`. `library-insight.json` is the intermediate.
- The denominator is exactly one input identity. The count is not a number of libraries, cells, corners or arcs checked.
- Only the literals `authoring-qualification` and `hima-library-insight-report/1` are qualified values. The identity is checked as *present and well-formed only*: the Pack recomputes no digest and claims the string identifies no artifact.
- Native QuaLib qualification, production Library facts and Wave 2 E1--E4 claims are outside this Pack's TEST.

**The boundary of one Campaign.**
- Input identity: exactly one Campaign-supplied local Library Insight authoring-qualification input carrying exactly the five declared fields and no additional opaque success value.
- Feedback that may change the next move: only the typed outcome of the generation. A refusal may be retried once on the identical input; no new, relaxed, edited or second input may enter the Campaign, and no field may be relaxed to make a value appear.
- Budget: Site `local`; 1 generation + 1 retry (the retry only when the first attempt produced no successful value); time box 300 s total, 120 s per attempt; no licence seat; no EDA wrapper; no network.
- The Golden Flow stays where it lies; a Campaign workspace never writes into it and the Pack copies no file of it.

**Source-linked counterexamples that later readers and rules must survive.** These are test input, not a claim that any commercial flow has passed.
1. Positive fixture — the all-`a` 64-hex digest with `authoring-qualification`, `hima-library-insight-report/1`, a non-blank provenance and two unknowns: both commands succeed and `library_contract_ready` = 1 (`flow/library-input.json`, line 2).
2. True refusal, empty list — `unknowns: []` makes `analyze-library-contract.sh` raise `invalid local Library authoring-qualification input`: non-zero exit, no result file, no numeric value (lines 19--22 of that script).
3. Missing field — no `provenance`, or a blank/whitespace provenance, is the same refusal (line 18).
4. Malformed identity — a 63-character, uppercase or non-hex `sourceSha256`, or a missing one, is the same refusal (lines 14--15).
5. Wrong label or schema — `qualification` other than `authoring-qualification`, or `reportSchema` other than `hima-library-insight-report/1`, is the same refusal (lines 16--17).
6. Corrupt intermediate — an intermediate whose `schema` is not `hima-library-insight-report/1`, or whose unknowns are empty or hold blank elements, makes `read-library-contract.py` raise `invalid local Library authoring-qualification result`: no `observation.json`, no value (lines 10--20 of that script).
7. Extra opaque success value — an intermediate carrying an additional `"qualified": true` key **still yields 1**, because only the five declared keys are validated (lines 8--18). The author settled this in the flow's favour, so a reader must never present that case as evidence of anything beyond the five fields.
8. Multiple targets — two source identities offered at once, or one `sourceSha256` that is a list rather than a string, fails the shape check (line 15) and must surface as a refusal, never as a count of two.

## Golden Flow

Read in place with read tools; not one file of it was copied into this Pack. The source package that carries it lies beside it at `/private/tmp/hima-l4-Busi3e/hima-home-PADRHy/workspace/library-authoring-source`.

**Flow root, as named by SOP.md:** `/private/tmp/hima-l4-Busi3e/hima-home-PADRHy/workspace/library-authoring-source/flow`

- `README.md` — the whole generation is two commands, `sh analyze-library-contract.sh library-input.json library-insight.json` then `python3 read-library-contract.py library-insight.json observation.json`, and the flow states it is local and non-commercial: `/private/tmp/hima-l4-Busi3e/hima-home-PADRHy/workspace/library-authoring-source/flow/README.md`
- `analyze-library-contract.sh` (33 lines) — command 1: reads the input, validates the five declared fields against the literals and the 64-lowercase-hex shape, and writes the intermediate with exactly those five keys, renaming `reportSchema` into `schema`; any failed check raises and writes nothing: `/private/tmp/hima-l4-Busi3e/hima-home-PADRHy/workspace/library-authoring-source/flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`
- `read-library-contract.py` (24 lines) — command 2 and the producer of the counted value: re-validates the intermediate's five keys and writes `observation.json` holding the single value `library_contract_ready`, unit `count`, value `1`; otherwise it raises and writes no output: `/private/tmp/hima-l4-Busi3e/hima-home-PADRHy/workspace/library-authoring-source/flow/read-library-contract.py`
- `library-input.json` (7 lines) — the flow's positive fixture: all-`a` digest placeholder, the label, the schema, a provenance line and two unknowns: `/private/tmp/hima-l4-Busi3e/hima-home-PADRHy/workspace/library-authoring-source/flow/library-input.json`

**Authoring authority lying beside the flow** (contents read; handed-off digests recorded as stated below).
- `SOP.md`, 23 lines, handed off as `06b4fe51d185cc716016eaa4616dd27b36e587deb398ace3f590e6b0c799d3aa`, 1286 bytes — states the Pack's limited purpose and names the adjacent `flow/` directory as the Golden Flow: `/private/tmp/hima-l4-Busi3e/hima-home-PADRHy/workspace/library-authoring-source/SOP.md`
- `qualification-requirements.md`, 15 lines, handed off as `7352d6a5656ccfcaa0c84de04e8433336f9e3870e241947ceeb6e34bdf942b73`, 691 bytes — the five checked values and the rule that a true count of one infers nothing: `/private/tmp/hima-l4-Busi3e/hima-home-PADRHy/workspace/library-authoring-source/qualification-requirements.md`
- `report-requirements.md`, 8 lines, handed off as `41b01f43906a6ff46b33639f2df5a15bf63eb0697439b086852b65089208428b`, 475 bytes — what the evidence envelope must retain and what the customer-facing wording must not claim: `/private/tmp/hima-l4-Busi3e/hima-home-PADRHy/workspace/library-authoring-source/report-requirements.md`

Those three digests are the values handed off to this session. This authoring session has no shell, so the digests were **not recomputed** here; the file contents above were read in place, and the digest values are recorded exactly as handed off rather than as verified by this stage.

## Answers

**Round 1 — the business.**
1. *What does one generation vary?* Recommended: nothing mechanical; the Pack declares zero strategy knobs and a generation varies only which single input is offered and whether it survives the five-field check. Answer: accepted with the bounded scope.
2. *What is measured, in what unit, read from where, by whom?* Recommended: `libraryContract` = `observation.json`, one value `library_contract_ready`, unit `count`, `1` only when the five result fields hold; the Pack's reader holds it against the declared literals and the Judge rules it against goal `1`; `library-insight.json` is an intermediate. Answer: accepted.
3. *What ends a Campaign of this Pack?* Recommended: goal met; converged on equality of a discrete value between the generation and its retry; refused by the flow as "no qualified measurement"; plus a reach-the-budget stop reported as unfinished. Answer: accepted — "the three stated endings".
4. *What must a person never have to guess?* Recommended: the five readings — one bounded local contract present and read; no value is not zero; the count comes from `observation.json`; the denominator is one input identity; only `authoring-qualification` and `hima-library-insight-report/1` are qualified. Answer: accepted.
5. *What bounds one Campaign?* Recommended: one Campaign-supplied input identity; feedback only from the typed outcome; Site `local`; 1 generation + 1 retry; a short time box; no licence. Answer: accepted — "one generation/one retry/300 s/no licence budget".
6. *Were the handed-off source digests recomputed?* Recommended: record them as the stated identity of what was read and say they were not recomputed here. Answer: accepted ("recommended").

**Round 2 — where the author's words and the flow disagree.**
7. *Extra opaque success values: flow ignores extras, the requirement file refuses them — which reading?* Recommended: follow the flow; the five named fields are the whole contract, the Pack's envelope carries exactly those five plus the single count, and the Pack claims no strictness the flow does not perform. Answer: accepted — the author explicitly accepted the flow's two-command generation and its behaviour.
8. *What is `sourceSha256` checked to be?* Recommended: present and 64 lowercase hex only; no digest recomputed and no claim that the string identifies an artifact. Answer: accepted.
9. *The schema field's two names?* Recommended: keep both as the flow has them — `reportSchema` in the input, `schema` in the envelope — and let the reader validate `schema`. Answer: accepted — "the envelope `schema` field".
10. *Confirm the ending set.* Recommended: the three endings above, with the generation limit kept as a budget reported as unfinished. Answer: confirmed — "the three stated endings".
11. *Budget numbers.* Recommended: Site `local`, 1 generation + 1 retry, retry only after a non-success on the identical input, no licence seat, no EDA wrapper, no network, and a 300 s total time box. Answer: accepted — "one generation/one retry/300 s/no licence budget".
12. *Are the handed-off digests recomputed?* Recommended: no — record them as handed off and say so. Answer: accepted, and no commercial Library fact was inferred at any point.

## Ambiguities resolved

1. **Extra opaque success values.** `qualification-requirements.md` says additional opaque success values are a Reader refusal/unknown, while `analyze-library-contract.sh` copies out only the five fields and `read-library-contract.py` validates only those five keys, so an intermediate carrying `"qualified": true` still yields 1. Put to the author as its own question; settled in the flow's favour — the five named fields are the whole contract, the Pack's report carries exactly those five values plus the single count and no success value of its own, and the tolerance is recorded in `Business` so no reader ever presents that case as qualified evidence.
2. **What `sourceSha256` establishes.** The SOP speaks of a source having a SHA-256 identity, while the flow checks presence and shape only and its own fixture is an all-`a` placeholder that digests no artifact. Settled: the Pack verifies the identity *field* (present, 64 lowercase hex) and recomputes no digest; the limitation is stated where the count is read, so "identity" is never read as an established artifact identity.
3. **One field, two names.** The input field is `reportSchema`; the intermediate's key is `schema`, and that is what the reader validates. Settled: both names are recorded as the flow has them and the Pack states the rename on its face, so a person never has to guess which name the result uses.
4. **The declared output name versus the file name.** The author required the reader-backed output to be declared exactly as `libraryContract`, while the flow's reader writes a file named `observation.json`. Settled: `libraryContract` is the declared output name, `observation.json` is the file that backs it, and `library-insight.json` is the intermediate that is never the measured value.
5. **"No success value" versus a report that must show something.** The author required invalid or absent input to have no success value, while a report normally shows a number. Settled: a refusal is realized as a non-zero exit with no output file, and the Campaign records "no qualified measurement" — never a `0` and never a failure count.
6. **"One generation" versus an honest convergence ending.** A 1-generation budget cannot be an ending, and a discrete value cannot converge gradually. Settled: convergence is declared as equality of the typed outcome between the generation and its retry, and the generation limit stays a budget whose exhaustion is reported as unfinished rather than as a conclusion.

## Knowledge applied

- `what-a-golden-flow-is.md` — kept the flow where it lies and made this record pointers only (the absolute paths and what was read there); no file of the flow was copied into the Pack, and reproducing the flow is not the goal.
- `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md` — forced the three endings to be named in the Pack's own words with the value that detects each (the count, the equality of the typed outcome, the flow's non-zero exit), and kept the 1-generation limit as a budget reported as "budget reached, unfinished".
- `assert-the-checker-options.md` — made the option set explicit beside the goal: the five declared names with their shapes and literals, and which reader holds the observed envelope against them; a mismatch is a blocker rather than a verdict, and the flow's identity is recorded so a later comparison can say what was checked.
- `one-checker-per-session.md` — kept one act node running the flow's two-command session with one reader and one named value (`library_contract_ready`), instead of splitting or summing counts; the value is named after the tool that produced it.
- `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md` — kept the requested goal (`1`), the observed value and the refusal distinct, so a malformed or absent input stays a retained shortfall rather than being massaged into a `0`, and no conclusion is drawn from a blocked or incomplete read.

Read but not applied: `attribute-by-database-relation.md` — this flow has no tool database and no instance-to-master relation, and no adoption question is asked, so it changed nothing here.

## Goal template

One target, bound when the Campaign starts, read on the verdict, and never widened by the Run.

- **`target_contract_count`** — unit **count**. It is the number of bounded local Library Insight authoring-qualification contracts this Campaign was started to find present and read in its one input. A Campaign of this Pack is started with `target_contract_count = 1`.
- **What it means.** The value it is judged against, `library_contract_ready` (unit `count`), is the number of bounded local authoring-qualification contracts that were present and read in full: `1` means that one contract was present and read, and it means nothing about a library.
- **Where it lands.** The goal rule `library-contract-ready-is-one@1` binds it as its threshold, so the number the person asked for sits on the verdict record beside the number that was read; a generation cannot widen the goal to manufacture a pass.
- **Precision and bounds.** Exact integer, unit `count`, no tolerance, no band, no rounding. The reader produces only `1` or an unknown, so the only qualifying value in this business is `1`; anything else is not a met goal and is not rounded into one.
- **Shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`** — it put the declared option list (the five checked fields, in the next section) beside this target, so the target is never read apart from the checks it was measured under.
- **Shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`** — it required the goal to be claimed only from a current valid measurement and the required Judge verdict, which is why the target is a bound threshold on a rule over a reader's value and not a sentence in a report.

## Constraints

Every constraint the goal carries, typed and checkable, with the options the measurement was made under.

1. **The option set the measurement was made under** (declared, not inferred): the intermediate result must carry exactly these five fields, with these shapes and literals — `sourceSha256`, a string matching exactly 64 lowercase hex characters; `qualification`, the literal `authoring-qualification`; `schema`, the literal `hima-library-insight-report/1`; `provenance`, a non-blank string; `unknowns`, a non-empty list whose every element is a non-blank string. The Pack's reader declares `emits: [library_contract_ready]` and the harness holds what the script actually writes against that declaration, so a reading under any other check set is a blocker and not a verdict.
2. **Local and non-commercial, typed as an absence of tools**: Site `local`; no Liberty file, no QuaLib, no `edarun`, no EDA wrapper, no network, no licence seat, no production Library facts, no E1--E4 requalification, no customer data. No Job of this Pack holds a licence.
3. **One input identity**: exactly one input, whose declared `sourceSha256` is present and well-formed. The Pack recomputes no digest and claims the string identifies no artifact. Two identities offered at once, or a `sourceSha256` that is not a string, is a refusal — never a count of two.
4. **Refusal, not zero**: a missing, malformed, refused or additional-field case is an explicit refusal or unknown value; it is never `0`, never `false`, never "failed qualification", and never a qualified measurement. The reader may write a typed zero only where a report proves zero, and nothing in this business proves zero.
5. **No inference**: a count of one licenses no claim about Library API, PVT, revision, design impact, quality, adoption or customer value, and no commercial qualification.
- **Shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`** — the option list is constraint 1, declared in the Pack beside the goal and asserted at run time before the count is read, as a typed value rather than a comment.
- **Shaped by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`** — constraint 4 keeps the refusal a retained shortfall: an incomplete read is recorded as no qualified measurement rather than massaged into a zero.

## Run contract

**Inputs a Site binds** (`bindings:` in that Site's own file, never in the Pack):
- `flowRoot` — the Golden Flow's root on the Site: `/private/tmp/hima-l4-Busi3e/hima-home-PADRHy/workspace/library-authoring-source/flow` on the local Site. Read-only to a Campaign, which runs in its own copy of the pieces named below and never in this directory.
- `libraryInput` — the one local Library Insight authoring-qualification input, a JSON file carrying exactly the five declared fields and no additional opaque success value. On the local Site this is the flow's own fixture `library-input.json`, whose declared `sourceSha256` is the all-`a` placeholder.
- `workspaceRoot` — where Campaign workspaces are created; the Permit must allow writes under it and the Pack writes nowhere else.

**What is copied into the Campaign workspace** (`<workspace>/flow/`, once per Campaign, by the runner; the Pack copies nothing itself): `analyze-library-contract.sh`, `read-library-contract.py`, `library-input.json`.

**Wrappers the Site's Permit must allow**: `sh`, the first word of both declared command lines, and `python3`, which both of them exec — the flow's own second command line begins with it. Nothing else is named, and a Site that allows neither cannot host this Pack.

**Tools** — each with the wrapper that section declares:
- `contract-check` — wrapper `sh`; file `tools/contract-check.sh`, written from the flow's own stated command line; argv is exactly the flow's command 1 against the Campaign's copy, `sh <workspace>/flow/analyze-library-contract.sh ${libraryInput} <workspace>/library-insight.json`, with no added argument and no environment override. A non-zero exit is the flow refusing the input: the generation's failed attempt, retried once, then a Hard blocker.
- **Reader** `library-contract-ready@1` — wrapper `sh`; file `tools/read-library-contract.sh`, this Pack's own script under its own `tools/`; argv runs the flow's command 2 as the flow states it, `python3 <workspace>/flow/read-library-contract.py ${REPORT} ${OUT}`. When the flow's script exits zero, the harness reads the envelope it wrote; when the flow refuses, this script writes the same single value type as an unknown, carrying the flow's own refusal sentence in `unknownReason`, and exits zero, so a refusal is a typed unknown and never a zero. `reportKind: library-contract-report`; `emits: [library_contract_ready]`.

**Outputs a generation leaves** (paths relative to the Campaign workspace):
- `libraryInsight` — `library-insight.json`; the intermediate between the flow's two commands; no reader; read by a person after a refusal, never judged.
- `libraryContract` — `observation.json`, reader `library-contract-ready`. This is the declared, reader-backed output of this Pack and the only judged one.

**Budget** — what bounds new attempts and generations:
- **one generation**: the graph does not loop; no edge revisits a node, so the Run makes one pass of the method;
- **one retry**: the Run's Retry allowance is `1`, so an attempt that fails is repeated once on the identical input. No new, relaxed, edited or second input may enter the Campaign;
- **time box** `300` s for the Campaign, with `120` s as this Pack's declared bound on one attempt;
- **no licence seat**, no commercial EDA wrapper, no network.

**Shaped by `what-a-golden-flow-is.md`** — the flow stays where it lies and this contract carries pointers to it and to the pieces the runner copies; not one file of it is written into the Pack.
**Shaped by `one-checker-per-session.md`** — one Job for the check, one reader for the value, and one named value, rather than a second counting tool or a summed total.

## Semantics

One value, and no other. Every name a rule or a chooser reads below is declared here.

- **`library_contract_ready`** — unit **count**. **Source**: this Pack's reader `library-contract-ready@1`, reading the declared output `libraryContract` (`observation.json`). **What it measures**: whether the one bounded local authoring-qualification contract was present and read in full — value `1` when the intermediate carried all five declared fields with the declared shapes and literals, which the flow's own reader re-validates before the envelope exists.
- **Zero and absence.** The reader never writes `0`. A value of `null` carries the flow's own `unknownReason` and means the result was refused; an absent value means no reading was taken at all. Both mean "no qualified measurement" and neither is a measured failure — a reader never substitutes zero or another default for a value it could not find.
- **Nothing else.** No field count, no severity, no boolean, no second number, and no value the readers do not produce.
- **Shaped by `one-checker-per-session.md`** — the value is named after the thing that produced it and is the only count in this method, so nothing can be summed across tools.
- **Shaped by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`** — the requested target, the observed value and the refusal are kept distinct, and the resolution of this count is the whole of it: there is no band and no rounding to hide a difference in.

## Judge rules

- **`library-contract-ready-is-one@1`** — this Pack's own rule, `rules/library-contract-ready-is-one.yml`. It requires `[{type: library_contract_ready}]`, its subject is the same value, and its predicate is `eq` against the threshold its `parameter` names, `target_contract_count`, in unit `count` (the rule's bound parameter, bound by the Run's goal, not a value read from an observation). PASS means the currently observed `library_contract_ready` equals the target the Run was started with — the goal is met, and nothing further is proposed.
- **FAIL** is not reachable in this method: the reader writes `1` or an unknown, never another number, so no observed count can fail this predicate. This Pack therefore draws no edge for FAIL, and a person should read that absence as a statement about the business, not as an omitted path.
- **UNDETERMINED** is reachable and is the refusal: no `library_contract_ready` was observed at all, or the observed one is `null`. The verdict cites the observation record it looked in and carries the reader's own `unknownReason` — the flow's refusal sentence — so the reason travels with the verdict. This Pack labels no edge for UNDETERMINED; the wait node below is where such a Run stops.
- **What each verdict cites**: the observation record id the value was read from, and the value as read. A verdict that could not read a value cites the observation it looked in and says why.
- **Shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`** — the rule is only applied over a reading whose option set (the five declared fields) was declared in advance, so a mismatch is a blocker with a sentence rather than a verdict.
- **Shaped by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`** — an absent or unknown value yields UNDETERMINED naming the reason, never a substituted zero that would read as a measured failure.

## Choosers

- **`contract-outcome@1`** — this Pack's own chooser, `choosers/contract-outcome.yml`. It declares no parameter, and it reads one thing: `ready: {type: library_contract_ready, unit: count}`.
- **Its one clause**: `when: {goal: PASS}` → `goalMet: true`. With the goal rule PASSing, the question the Campaign was started for is answered, and the chooser proposes no next move.
- **Why there is no second clause.** This Pack declares no strategy knob, and a clause's `next` must set at least one knob — a `next` that changed nothing would be a Loop revisiting its act nodes with the Strategy that just ran. With no knob to set, the honest chooser has exactly one thing to say.
- **Why the explore node declares no convergence.** Convergence is the harness's arithmetic over a chooser's own read across *earlier generations*, and a Pack with no `next` opens exactly one generation, so there is no second measurement to compare and a `converge:` block here would be an ending nothing can reach. The generation limit, the Retry allowance and the time box remain budgets.
- **Shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`** — convergence is stated in the chooser's own vocabulary or not at all, and the generation limit stays a budget rather than being dressed as a conclusion.

## Endings

Two ways a Campaign of this Pack ends, and one budget stop that is not an ending.

1. **Goal met** — reached by the chooser's `when: {goal: PASS}` clause returning `goalMet: true`, on a PASS of `library-contract-ready-is-one` over an observed `library_contract_ready` of `1`. The Run ends holding the value, the observation record that carried it, and the bound target it was judged against.
2. **Refused by the Golden Flow** — this Pack's own ending, reached at the `blocked` wait node, to which nothing draws an edge: the fabric routes a Hard blocker there, and it is reached when the flow's own command exits non-zero on every attempt the Retry allowance allows, or when `library-contract-ready-is-one` returns UNDETERMINED and no edge is labelled for it. The Run stops there for a person, and every face says "no qualified measurement" — never `0`, never a failed qualification.
3. **Budget reached, unfinished — not an ending.** If the one generation, its one retry and the 300 s box are spent with neither of the above, the report says plainly that the budget was reached, shows the attempt that failed and its refusal sentence, and claims no conclusion.

**One departure from the intent record, stated plainly.** The record's second ending, *converged* (the generation and its retry returning the identical typed outcome), is **not declared here**. This Pack declares no strategy knob, a chooser clause's `next` must set at least one, and the harness's convergence is arithmetic over successive generations of a Loop; with one generation there is no second measurement to compare, so a convergence ending could never be reached and declaring one would be exactly the contradiction this stage exists to catch. The record's own third ending — the refusal, which the record describes as the flow exiting non-zero with no successful value — covers the honest stop this business actually has. Reinstating a convergence ending would require a declared strategy knob the author explicitly declined, so it is the author's to decide, not this stage's.
- **Shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`** — every ending above is one a value or a verdict actually reaches, is named in this Pack's own words, and the budget is reported as a budget; the ending nothing could reach was dropped rather than declared.

## Workshops

**None.** No model writes code at run time in this method. The generation is the Golden Flow's own command line, and the reading is this Pack's own reader script — a static file of the Pack's `tools/` written at authoring time, launched by the harness with the paths the Permit already decided. The author asked for a bounded local qualification check, not for code written during a Campaign, so there is no workshop, and there is no output a workshop would have to declare in `Semantics`.
- **No knowledge file shaped this section**: it records what the author's scope leaves out, and that scope comes from the intent record's `Business` and `Answers`, not from a knowledge file.

## Knowledge

**This Pack declares no knowledge file of its own**, and its contract names none: there is no `knowledge/` file for a Model moment to read, because this method runs no Model moment. The limited scope the source package requires — that only a local authoring-qualification input is checked, and that native QuaLib qualification, production Library facts and Wave 2 E1--E4 claims are outside this Pack's test — is stated in the Pack's own intent, specification and test record, where a person reads it, rather than in a file nothing would open.
- **No knowledge file shaped this section**: it states an absence. The knowledge that shaped the rest of this specification sits in the authoring chain, beside the sections it changed, and `what-a-golden-flow-is.md` is why the Pack carries pointers and pointers only rather than an essay about the flow.

# and it claims no commercial qualification. The Golden Flow stays where it lies; a Campaign runs in
# its own copy of the three files named under `workspace.copy:`.

version: '1'
title: Library Insight authoring-qualification check

# What a Site binds, in its own site file under `bindings:`. The same pack runs on another Site by

  - name: flowRoot
    description: >-

  - name: libraryInput
    description: >-
      The one local Library Insight authoring-qualification input this Campaign checks: a JSON file

  - name: workspaceRoot
    description: >-
      Where Campaign workspaces are created. The Site's Permit must allow writes under it; nothing

# What one generation leaves in its Campaign workspace, relative to the workspace root.
outputs:
  - name: libraryContract
    path: library-insight.json
    reader: library-contract-ready
    description: >-
      The local Library Insight authoring-qualification result the flow's first command wrote in this
      Campaign's own copy — the file the flow calls library-insight.json. This pack's own reader
      turns it into the single value `library_contract_ready`, running the flow's own second command

      file; a reading of it means only that this bounded source contract was present and read.

    - read-library-contract.py
    - library-input.json

# The pack's tools. Each names the file a person reads and runs by hand, and the command line the

tools:
  - id: contract-check
    file: tools/contract-check.sh
    description: >-
      One generation's check: the Golden Flow's own first command line, run in the Campaign's own
      copy of the flow. A non-zero exit is the flow refusing this input — a failed attempt, retried

# Every rule this pack's judge nodes may apply, by reference: this folder's rules/ first, the
# bundle's second.
rules:
  - library-contract-ready-is-one

# What a person reads each number under: the one goal parameter the graph binds.

# The library-authoring-qualification check as a HimaFabric graph: one generation runs the Golden
# Flow's own first command on the one bound input, reads the result it wrote into the single value
# `library_contract_ready`, judges that value against the declared goal of one, and either ends
# because the goal is met or stops at the wait node for a person.
#
# There is no loop and no revisit edge: a chooser clause's `next` must set at least one strategy
# knob, this pack declares none, and so a Campaign of it opens exactly one generation.
id: library-authoring-qualification
version: '1'
entry: check-contract

nodes:
  # Act: run the pack's tool on the Site, in the Campaign's own copy of the flow, and wait for it.
  - id: check-contract
    kind: act
    parameters:
      tool: contract-check

  # Act: read the result that generation wrote into HimaLedger, through this pack's own reader.

  # Judge: the one rule, over the value the reader produced and the goal the Run bound. PASS leaves

# the contract pointed it at, the file it must write, and the Campaign root. Its first word is the
# wrapper the Site's Permit decides on.

file: tools/read-library-contract.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""This pack's own reader for the declared output `libraryContract`.

The harness launches it as

    python3 ${READER} ${REPORT} ${OUT} ${WORKSPACE}

so ``sys.argv[1]`` is the observed local Library Insight authoring-qualification result (the file the
Golden Flow calls ``library-insight.json``), ``sys.argv[2]`` is the file this script must write, and
``sys.argv[3]`` is the Campaign root, whose ``flow/`` copy holds the Golden Flow's own reader.

It runs the Golden Flow's own second command line exactly as that flow states it —
``python3 <flow>/read-library-contract.py <report> <out>`` — so the validation of the five declared
fields stays the flow's, and the reading document the flow writes is this script's output.

When the flow refuses the result, this script writes the same single value type as an explicit
unknown, carrying the flow's own sentence in ``unknownReason``, and exits 0. That is the honest third
answer: no success value, and never a zero standing in for a number nobody read.
"""

import json
import subprocess
import sys

report, out, workspace = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
flow_reader = workspace.rstrip("/") + "/flow/read-library-contract.py"

run = subprocess.run(
    [sys.executable or "python3", flow_reader, report, out],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
if run.returncode == 0:
    sys.exit(0)

reason = (run.stderr or run.stdout or "").strip() or (
    "the local Library authoring-qualification result was refused by the flow's own reader"
)
document = {
    "values": [
        {
            "type": "library_contract_ready",
            "unit": "count",
            "value": None,
            "unknownReason": reason,
        }
    ]
}
with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    json.dump(document, handle)
    handle.write("\n")

1: # Over-constrain, and read the violation
2: 
3: A passing timing constraint establishes closure at the tested target and conditions. Preserve the
4: actual reported slack, whether zero or positive. Some synthesis flows report zero once a target is
5: met; that zero does not establish the fastest achievable implementation. A pass alone does not
6: prove global optimality, and a negative slack does not prove the tool exhausted every strategy.
7: 
8: A setup violation is a measured shortfall. For an asked period P and slack V < 0, P + |V| can guide
9: the next trial when the timing model makes that approximation useful. It remains a hypothesis:
10: resynthesis, path changes, and period-dependent IO delays or clock latency can change the result.
11: Only a new valid trial can establish closure at its tested period.
12: 
13: ## What this means for a Pack
14: 
15: - Keep the requested target, reported clock period, actual slack and proposed next target distinct.
16:   Check the report's units, scope and conditions before using it in a decision.
17: - A deliberately tighter first trial can expose a shortfall; a passing trial is still useful
18:   evidence. Choose the initial pressure from the business question and available budget.
19: - A Pack may recommend `P + |V| - step` after failure and `P - step` after a passing trial that
20:   misses Goal. Do not systematically relax a zero-slack passing trial by adding a guard band.
21:   Validate every candidate against the Pack's bounds and precision before launching it.
22: - Use the tool's actual reporting precision. Repeated rounded values can hide differences;
23:   convergence is limited to the observed resolution and tested conditions.
24: - State: “Trial X measured slack Y; the next proposed period is Z and remains untested.”
25:   Claim Goal met only from current, valid measurements and the required Judge verdicts.
26: - Execution faults, incomplete reports and changed inputs cannot support a design conclusion.
27:   Retain the failure and resolve it before deriving the next strategy.
28: 
29: ## Source and limits
30: 
31: The reference opene902 stand-in exposed a chooser that relaxed the period on every zero-slack pass.
32: That counterexample motivated the over-constraining recommendation. It does not establish that
33: all tools always report zero, or that one failed synthesis reveals the exact achievable period.
34: When citing this file, identify the recommendation used and the actual evidence behind the decision.

(End of file - total 34 lines)
</content>

1: # End honestly, and in more than one way
2: 
3: A Campaign ends in facts. There are exactly three honest ways for one to end, and a generation limit
4: is not among them.
5: 
6: 1. **The Goal is met.** The target was reached and the constraints hold, stated with the values and
7:    the citations that say so.
8: 2. **The exploration converged.** The moves stopped changing anything: the value the Loop converges
9:    on stayed inside the declared band across the declared number of generations. "Converged" is a
10:    measurement, not a mood — the pack declares which value and which band.
11: 3. **An ending the pack declares in its own words.** Something in the business said stop, and the
12:    pack said in advance what that would be: a gate the library tool refuses to pass, adoption that
13:    stayed at zero, an input the flow rejects, a stage that cannot run on this Site at all.
14: 
15: **A generation limit is a budget, not an ending.** When a Campaign stops because it ran out of
16: generations, nobody knows what happened: the method may have been converging slowly, or it may have
17: been walking away from the answer for its whole life. An ending nobody can explain is the one thing a
18: Campaign must not deliver, because the whole promise is that it ends in facts.
19: 
20: ## What this means for a pack you are authoring
21: 
22: - **Write the `Endings` section first, not last.** Every way this business can stop, in the words a
23:   person would use. If you cannot name three, you do not yet know the business well enough to author
24:   the pack.
25: - **Every declared ending needs the value that detects it.** An ending that no reader produces a
26:   number for is an ending the runner can never reach. If the pack says "stop when the library gate
27:   fails", some reader has to report whether the gate failed.
28: - **Convergence is stated in the chooser's own vocabulary.** The value converged on has to be one
29:   the chooser actually reads; a pack that converges on a number its chooser never looks at can only
30:   ever end at its limit.
31: - **The generation limit stays, and stays a budget.** It protects the Site and the person's time. It
32:   should be reached only when something is wrong, and when it is reached the report says so plainly
33:   rather than dressing it up as a conclusion.
34: - **Say what a person must never have to guess.** If a stop can be read two ways — met exactly, or
35:   not measured at all — the pack's words must distinguish them on every face.
36: 
37: ## Citing it
38: 
39: When this file shaped a decision, cite it by name and say what it changed — "made every ending one
40: this pack declares in words, and added the reader that detects the library gate's refusal".

(End of file - total 40 lines)
</content>

1: # Assert the verification tool's options before the run counts
2: 
3: A verification session answers the question its options asked, not the question you meant. The same
4: tool, on the same data, with a different rule deck, a different cell view, a different set of checks
5: enabled or a different severity threshold, will answer "clean" and "not clean" with equal confidence
6: — and both answers are correct for what was actually asked.
7: 
8: **So a run whose options were not asserted has not verified anything.** It has produced a number
9: whose meaning nobody can state afterwards, and a pass obtained under the wrong options is worse than
10: a failure: it is a failure that looks like success and travels into a report as a fact.
11: 
12: ## What this means for a pack you are authoring
13: 
14: - **Declare the options in the pack, beside the constraint they serve.** Which checks, which rule
15:   set, which views, which thresholds. Not "the usual ones" — the list, written down.
16: - **Assert them at run time, before the count is read.** The session must be made to state the
17:   options it ran under, and a reader must hold that statement against the declaration. If the two
18:   disagree, the generation has no verdict: it has a blocker, and the pack says so in words.
19: - **Make the assertion a typed value, not a comment.** "Options as declared: yes/no", plus the list
20:   the session reported, so the judge can cite it and a person reading the report six months later can
21:   see exactly what was checked.
22: - **Never infer the options from the result.** A clean result is not evidence that the right checks
23:   ran; it is equally consistent with no checks having run at all.
24: - **Record the tool's own version beside them.** Options mean different things across versions, and a
25:   Campaign compared against an earlier one has to be able to say whether that comparison is fair.
26: 
27: ## The failure this prevents
28: 
29: A generation passes; the report says the design is clean; the option set had one whole class of check
30: switched off. Nothing in the ledger is wrong — every number is what the tool said — and the
31: conclusion is false. There is no way to detect this later from the numbers alone, which is why the
32: assertion has to happen before the count is read rather than after the campaign is over.
33: 
34: ## Citing it
35: 
36: When this file shaped a decision, cite it by name and say what it changed — "added the declared
37: option list to the run contract and an assertion reader that fails the generation when the session
38: reports anything else".

(End of file - total 38 lines)
</content>

1: # One verification tool per session
2: 
3: A count belongs to one tool and one option set. Run two verification tools in one session and the
4: violation count that comes out belongs to neither: you cannot say which tool found what, you cannot
5: compare the number against a run of either tool alone, and you cannot re-run half of it.
6: 
7: **So a session runs one verification tool.** Not one *kind* of tool — one tool. If the business needs
8: two, that is two act nodes, two sessions, two reports and two typed values.
9: 
10: ## What this means for a pack you are authoring
11: 
12: - **One act node per verification tool.** Each node launches its own session, produces its own
13:   report, and its report is read by its own reader into its own named value. The node's name says
14:   which tool it is.
15: - **Name the values after what produced them.** Two values both called "violations" will be compared
16:   by somebody. Give each the tool's name in its own name, and its unit and meaning in the pack's
17:   `Semantics`.
18: - **Do not sum across tools.** A total over two tools' counts is a number with no unit and no owner.
19:   If the business wants one verdict, the judge takes it from a rule over the two named values, and
20:   the rule says in words how the two combine.
21: - **Fork rather than fold.** Two verification tools that can run at once are two branches of a fork
22:   that converge into a judge node — that is what fork and join are for, and it keeps each count
23:   attached to the session that produced it.
24: - **One session, one option set.** The companion rule is in `assert-the-checker-options.md`: a
25:   session whose options were not asserted has verified nothing, and a session running two tools
26:   cannot have one asserted option set at all.
27: 
28: ## The failure this prevents
29: 
30: A single session runs two tools to save a licence checkout; the report carries one count; six months
31: later a person asks which tool found the seventeen violations and no record can answer. The Campaign
32: ended in a number rather than in facts.
33: 
34: ## Citing it
35: 
36: When this file shaped a decision, cite it by name and say what it changed — "split the one
37: verification node into two, one per tool, each with its own reader and its own named count, joined at
38: a judge node".

(End of file - total 38 lines)
</content>
